thread:
Maya L.: sharing a quick design review for the API Keys list. Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE (frame: 'Key List / Row Actions'). Maya L.: Main asks: where should the primary action live (left vs right), how to present Rotate vs Disable vs Revoke, and what the empty state copy should say for org admins vs members. Screenshots in thread. Sam K.: My vote: primary CTA = Create API key on the left. It's the most common entry. Keep Rotate lower-profile. Sam K.: Suggestion: move Rotate into the kebab and expose a tiny inline pill for keys with auto-rotate enabled. Aisha R.: Copy thinking: use "Disable temporarily" for recoverable actions and reserve "Revoke" or "Permanently revoke" for non-recoverable. Keeps tone clearer for non-technical users. Aisha R.: Example modal heading: "Permanently revoke this API key?" and supporting line: "This will immediately stop any requests using the key." Julian M.: Accessibility checklist: when modals open, focus should go to the dialog title, set aria-modal="true", trap focus, and label the close button. For success toasts use role="status" aria-live="polite"; for errors use aria-live="assertive". Julian M.: Snippet we can reuse: ```
Key disabled — undo
``` Oliver B.: Backend note: 'last used' and per-key traffic metrics exist but are costly for a full table render. We can lazy-load these per page or on hover. Oliver B.: Implementation plan: render primary table, then fetch last-used for visible rows and fill in skeletons. I'll add a /keys/last-used batch endpoint. design-bot: Running microcopy A/B: variant A uses "Deactivate" for soft actions, variant B uses "Disable" (experiment_id: key_microcopy_47). Maya L.: Proposed UI changes: - Primary CTA: "Create API key" (primary, left) - Row actions: visible kebab menu -> Rotate, Disable/Deactivate (soft), Permanently revoke (danger) inside menu - Revoke modal copy: "This will stop all requests immediately. This action cannot be undone." Danger CTA: "Permanently revoke key" (red). - Undo toast after revoke: "Key revoked — undo" (10s). If user clicks undo we show "Key restored" toast. Maya L.: Empty state variants: - Org admin: "No API keys yet. Create a key to start sending requests to Redwood." CTA: "Create API key"; secondary: "Rotation & policy docs". - Member: "You don't have any API keys. Ask an admin to create one or request access." CTA: "Request key" (link to request flow). Sam K.: Add a small rotation-warning chip on keys older than 90 days. Hover shows suggested next-steps. Aisha R.: Tone nits: prefer plain verbs "Create" "Rotate" "Disable" over nouny / passive copy. Keeps CTAs clear. Julian M.: Keyboard nav: kebab must be reachable via Tab and activated with Enter/Space. Menu item order should be Rotate, Disable, Revoke. Focus ring visible on all interactive items. Oliver B.: Undo semantics: we already have soft-delete in the API. I'll add an endpoint to extend the soft-delete window so undo works reliably for 10s. Purge job will run later. Maya L.: Mobile note: increase kebab tappable area to 44x44 and consider moving primary CTA into a sticky footer on small screens. Sam K.: UX detail: when showing skeletons for last-used, include a subtle shimmer and keep layout stable to avoid content shift. Aisha R.: Legal requested stronger language for permanent actions. I'll prepare two variants for legal review: one using "Permanently revoke" and one using "Permanently deactivate". Julian M.: I'll schedule a quick screen-reader and keyboard pass after the next mock is uploaded. design-bot: Experiment rollout planned Fri 14:00 UTC for CTA ordering test (experiment id: keys_cta_order_303). Maya L.: Thanks all — I'll iterate the Figma, add the a11y checklist, and post an updated mock by EOD Wednesday. Drop any last-call comments there.
